# disrobe

> One tool to decompile, deobfuscate, and unpack compiled software, deterministically, in a single Rust binary. disrobe is a multi-language decompiler, deobfuscator, and unpacker covering Python, JavaScript, WebAssembly, .NET, JVM, Android, Go, Lua, PHP, Ruby, native PE/ELF/Mach-O, and more, behind one CLI with a deterministic pass pipeline that records exactly what it recovered and what it could not.

Recovery is always measured against an independent reference, never the tool's own output, and lossy results are reported as measured. The hosted docs live at https://1-3-7.github.io/disrobe/latest/ and a browser playground at https://1-3-7.github.io/disrobe/playground/.

disrobe is licensed under the Elastic License 2.0 (source-available; free to use, copy, modify, and self-host, with no rebranding and no offering as a hosted service). The name "disrobe" is reserved. A full single-file copy of these docs for ingestion lives at https://1-3-7.github.io/disrobe/llms-full.txt.

## Getting started

- [Introduction and capability overview](https://1-3-7.github.io/disrobe/latest/index.html): what disrobe decompiles, deobfuscates, and unpacks, and where its honest limits are.
- [Installation](https://1-3-7.github.io/disrobe/latest/installation.html): prebuilt binaries from GitHub Releases or build from source with one Rust toolchain.
- [Quickstart](https://1-3-7.github.io/disrobe/latest/quickstart.html): the disrobe auto command fingerprints an input and chains the right passes end to end.

## Architecture

- [Architecture overview](https://1-3-7.github.io/disrobe/latest/architecture.html): the workspace of Rust crates and the bytes-in, passes, emit recovery shape.
- [The five-rung IR ladder](https://1-3-7.github.io/disrobe/latest/ir-ladder.html): how artifacts are lifted from raw bytes up to recovered source.
- [Passes and the capability model](https://1-3-7.github.io/disrobe/latest/passes.html): the unit of work each transform performs and how capabilities are declared.
- [The chain runner](https://1-3-7.github.io/disrobe/latest/chain.html): how passes are detected and composed into an end-to-end recovery.
- [The .dr envelope](https://1-3-7.github.io/disrobe/latest/envelope.html): content-addressed caching of intermediate recovery state.
- [Metadata sidecar and provenance](https://1-3-7.github.io/disrobe/latest/llm-sidecar.html): deterministic metadata bundles and line-level provenance tracked separately from recovered output.

## Reverse-engineering toolkit

- [Supported families catalog](https://1-3-7.github.io/disrobe/latest/catalog.html): every packer, obfuscator, and bytecode format disrobe recognizes, per language, with what it recovers and where it walls.
- [Anti-analysis defeat](https://1-3-7.github.io/disrobe/latest/anti-analysis.html): how disrobe strips anti-debug, anti-VM, and obfuscation guards statically, without running the sample.
- [Queryable IR and capabilities](https://1-3-7.github.io/disrobe/latest/query.html): the disrobe query subcommand over recovered functions, calls, cross-references, string decoders, and capabilities.

## Language and format guides

- [Python decompiler](https://1-3-7.github.io/disrobe/latest/languages/python.html): in-house Rust pyc decompiler, pyarmor unpacker, pyinstaller and Nuitka extractors, and pickle analysis.
- [JavaScript and TypeScript deobfuscator](https://1-3-7.github.io/disrobe/latest/languages/javascript.html): deobfuscates obfuscated JS/TS, unbundles webpack output, and inspects packaged JS runtimes.
- [WebAssembly decompiler](https://1-3-7.github.io/disrobe/latest/languages/wasm.html): lifts Wasm modules to readable surfaces, reverses Wasm obfuscators, and decodes the Component Model and GC types.
- [JVM and Android decompiler](https://1-3-7.github.io/disrobe/latest/languages/jvm-android.html): Java class and DEX/Dalvik recovery to readable source.
- [.NET and CIL decompiler](https://1-3-7.github.io/disrobe/latest/languages/dotnet.html): managed assembly decompilation and deobfuscation.
- [Native PE, ELF, and Mach-O unpacking](https://1-3-7.github.io/disrobe/latest/languages/native.html): UPX and packer unpacking, symbol recovery, chain detection, and headless Ghidra decompile.
- [Go decompiler](https://1-3-7.github.io/disrobe/latest/languages/go.html): Go binary symbol and structure recovery.
- [Lua decompiler](https://1-3-7.github.io/disrobe/latest/languages/lua.html): Lua bytecode decompilation across versions.
- [PHP](https://1-3-7.github.io/disrobe/latest/languages/php.html): PHP source and bytecode recovery.
- [Ruby decompiler](https://1-3-7.github.io/disrobe/latest/languages/ruby.html): Ruby source recovery.
- [BEAM (Erlang and Elixir)](https://1-3-7.github.io/disrobe/latest/languages/beam.html): BEAM bytecode lifting to Erlang and Elixir.
- [Swift and Objective-C](https://1-3-7.github.io/disrobe/latest/languages/swift.html): Swift and Objective-C class dump and source recovery.
- [ActionScript 3 and Flash](https://1-3-7.github.io/disrobe/latest/languages/as3.html): SWF and ABC decompilation to ActionScript.
- [Mobile (Hermes and Flutter)](https://1-3-7.github.io/disrobe/latest/languages/mobile.html): Hermes bytecode and Flutter snapshot analysis.
- [Python pickle analysis](https://1-3-7.github.io/disrobe/latest/languages/pickle.html): scans pickle streams for malicious reduce callables without executing them.
- [Shell and PowerShell deobfuscation](https://1-3-7.github.io/disrobe/latest/languages/shell.html): unravels obfuscated shell and PowerShell scripts.
- [Containers and archives](https://1-3-7.github.io/disrobe/latest/languages/containers.html): unpacks installers, container images, and archive formats.

## CLI reference

- [CLI overview](https://1-3-7.github.io/disrobe/latest/cli/overview.html): the disrobe pass action input shape shared by every command.
- [Global flags](https://1-3-7.github.io/disrobe/latest/cli/global-flags.html): flags available across all passes.
- [Command reference](https://1-3-7.github.io/disrobe/latest/cli/reference.html): full per-pass command and action listing.
- [Project configuration](https://1-3-7.github.io/disrobe/latest/cli/config.html): the disrobe config file for repeatable runs.
- [Batch directory processing](https://1-3-7.github.io/disrobe/latest/cli/batch.html): recover a whole directory tree in one invocation.
- [Run reports](https://1-3-7.github.io/disrobe/latest/cli/report.html): machine-readable reports of what each run recovered.
- [Analysis-depth commands](https://1-3-7.github.io/disrobe/latest/cli/analysis-depth.html): strings, entropy, IOC, and YARA-style triage commands.
- [Diff and guard tooling](https://1-3-7.github.io/disrobe/latest/cli/diff-guard.html): diff recovered output and guard against regressions.
- [The daemon: HTTP, gRPC, LSP, MCP](https://1-3-7.github.io/disrobe/latest/cli/serve.html): long-running server exposing disrobe over four transports.

## Integrations

- [Use disrobe as a Rust library](https://1-3-7.github.io/disrobe/latest/library.html): embed disrobe's passes and chain runner directly in a Rust program.
- [Python bindings](https://1-3-7.github.io/disrobe/latest/python-bindings.html): drive disrobe passes from Python.
- [GitHub Action](https://1-3-7.github.io/disrobe/latest/integrations/github-action.html): run disrobe in CI.
- [pre-commit hook](https://1-3-7.github.io/disrobe/latest/integrations/pre-commit.html): block obfuscated or packed artifacts at commit time.
- [MCP server](https://1-3-7.github.io/disrobe/latest/integrations/mcp.html): a Model Context Protocol server for deobfuscation and decompilation tools. Analysis tools take inline base64 bytes and return structured JSON.

## Malware analysis and safety

- [Forensics and malware-safety posture](https://1-3-7.github.io/disrobe/latest/forensics-safety.html): exactly what does and does not execute, for analysts running hostile input without detonating it.
- [Threat model](https://1-3-7.github.io/disrobe/latest/threat-model.html): the attacker model disrobe defends against and its trust boundaries.

- [The disrobe playground](https://1-3-7.github.io/disrobe/playground/): decompile a .pyc, scan a pickle, and summarize a .wasm entirely client-side in the browser.
